title: Systematic review of rodent studies on deep brain stimulation targeting the striatum
title_zh: 啮齿类动物中针对纹状体深部脑刺激的系统评价
abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for treatment-resistant psychiatric disorders. Among the most investigated targets are striatal regions, which play central roles in cortico-striatal circuits involved in motivation, emotion, and cognition. However, evidence from rodent studies remains fragmented across target regions, behavioral domains, and stimulation protocols. We systematically reviewed preclinical studies investigating the behavioral effects of striatal DBS in rodents, focusing on anatomical targets, stimulation parameters, and behavioral outcomes. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed and Scopus were searched. Experimental studies evaluating striatal electrical DBS in rats or mice with behavioral outcomes were included. Data were extracted on animal characteristics, targeted striatal subregions, stimulation parameters, behavioral assessments, and main findings. Sixty-eight articles met the inclusion criteria. Most targeted the nucleus accumbens, particularly the shell and core, whereas the dorsal and mid striatum were comparatively underrepresented. Behavioral assessments were grouped into seven functional categories, with positive valence, negative valence systems and motor and locomotor activity being the most frequently investigated. Across studies, reported behavioral effects varied according to the stimulated subregion, behavioral paradigm, baseline state, disease model, and stimulation protocol. Qualitative patterns suggested that DBS often attenuated experimentally disrupted behavior, although substantial methodological heterogeneity limited direct comparisons. Overall, the evidence suggests that the behavioral effects of striatal DBS are context-dependent, reflecting the functional specificity of distinct striatal subregions. Future studies incorporating precise targeting, systematic parameter comparisons, adaptive stimulation approaches, and greater consideration of biological sex will strengthen the translational value of rodent DBS research.
abstract_zh: 深部脑刺激（DBS）已成为难治性精神障碍治疗的一种有前景的策略。其中，纹状体区域是研究最多的靶点之一，在参与动机、情绪和认知的皮质纹状体回路中发挥核心作用。然而，啮齿类动物研究的证据在不同靶点区域、行为领域和刺激方案方面仍分散不一。我们系统地回顾了研究啮齿类动物中纹状体DBS行为影响的临床前研究，重点关注解剖靶点、刺激参数和行为结局。按照PRISMA指南，在PubMed和Scopus中进行检索。纳入评估啮齿类动物中纹状体电学DBS行为结局的实验研究。提取了动物特征、靶向纹状体亚区域、刺激参数、行为评估和主要研究结果的数据。共68篇文章符合纳入标准。大多数研究靶向核accumbens，特别是壳部和核部，而背侧和中部纹状体则相对研究不足。行为评估被分为七个功能类别，其中正价性、负价性系统以及运动和运动活动的研究最为频繁。各研究中报告的行为影响根据刺激的亚区域、行为范式、基线状态、疾病模型和刺激方案而有所不同。质性模式表明，DBS通常能减轻实验性干扰的行为，但方法学上的显著异质性限制了直接比较。总体而言，证据表明，纹状体DBS的行为影响具有情境依赖性，反映了不同纹状体亚区域的功能特异性。未来结合精准靶向、系统性参数比较、自适应刺激方法以及更多考虑生物学性别的研究，将增强啮齿类动物DBS研究的转化价值。
